definitions.explanation: In Buddhism, mental states such as greed, anger, and delusion that cause suffering and hinder enlightenment. In everyday usage, refers more broadly to temptations and desires that are hard to resist.

examples.japanese: {煩悩|ぼんのう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{捨|す}てる→捨てる：00892_suteru⟧。
⟦ダイエット→ダイエット：17678_daietto⟧⟦{中|ちゅう}→〜中：09840_chuu⟧な⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{甘|あま}い{物|もの}→甘い物：20464_amaimono⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{食|た}べたい→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。{煩悩|ぼんのう}⟦だらけ→〜だらけ：18372_darake⟧だ。
examples.english: I want to eat sweets even though I'm on a diet. I'm full of temptations.

examples.japanese: ⟦{大晦日|おおみそか}→大晦日：05810_oomisoka⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{除夜|じょや}の{鐘|かね}→除夜の鐘：16977_joyanokane⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{百八|ひゃくはち}つ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{煩悩|ぼんのう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{払|はら}う→払う：00535_harau⟧⟦ため→ため：01145_tame⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{百八回|ひゃくはっかい}⟦{鳴|な}らされる→鳴らす：02381_narasu⟧。
examples.english: The New Year's Eve bell is rung 108 times to dispel the 108 worldly desires.

notes:
{煩悩|ぼんのう} originates from Buddhist terminology. In Buddhist thought, there are traditionally 108 {煩悩|ぼんのう}, which is why the ⟦{除夜|じょや}の{鐘|かね}→除夜の鐘：16977_joyanokane⟧ (New Year's Eve bell) is rung 108 times.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {煩悩|ぼんのう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{捨|す}てる→捨てる：00892_suteru⟧ (to abandon worldly desires)
- {煩悩|ぼんのう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{断|た}つ→断つ：27885_tatsu⟧ (to cut off worldly desires)
- {煩悩|ぼんのう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{打|う}ち{勝|か}つ→打ち勝つ：12768_uchikatsu⟧ (to overcome temptation)
- {煩悩|ぼんのう}⟦だらけ→〜だらけ：18372_darake⟧ (full of worldly desires)

USAGE:
While the word comes from serious Buddhist philosophy, it is commonly used in a light, self-deprecating way in everyday speech — for example, when someone cannot resist food or shopping. The humorous tone acknowledges human weakness without deep religious connotation.
